description: Recorded CLI argument shapes for @jorisjonkers-dev/deploy-config-schema, derived from src/deployment/commands.ts and src/cli.ts in that repository. Any change to the flags used in actions/deploy-artifact/run.sh or actions/deploy-preview/run.sh must be reflected here first; a subcommand invoked by either script with no entry here fails the completeness test. The filename carries no version so that bumping the pinned toolkit does not require renaming this fixture.

notes: The second positional is the deploy directory (e.g. 'deploy'), NOT the deployment.yml file.
The CLI routes to runFragmentRender when the first positional resolves to a fragment adapter.
context must be passed either as --context-dir (local dir containing cluster-context-public.yml) or as --context <digest-ref> plus --context-path <local-file>.
--schema-version does NOT exist in this subcommand; do not pass it.
--context is required (path to the pulled cluster-context-public.yml file).
--context-ref is required (the OCI digest ref string, e.g. ghcr.io/...@sha256:...).
The subcommand is 'artifact emit-contract' (two words after deploy-config-schema).
Takes a single --env per invocation; call once per environment.
Lifts the Kubernetes objects out of kubernetes-workload-fragment.yaml into one document per object plus a kustomization.yaml, so an OCIRepository plus Kustomization pair can apply the artifact.
The remaining fragments carry intent that aggregates across services and are reported as skipped, not emitted.
Invoked only when the apply-bundle input is true, because it does not exist before 0.20.0.
No published version of the toolkit provides this subcommand: grepping the packaged dist of 0.16.0 and 0.19.0 finds no reference to validate-raw-manifests.
The call is reached only when <deploy-dir>/raw-manifests exists, and no service repository has that directory, so the path has never executed.

Recorded as unimplemented rather than removed so the gap is visible: a repository that adds raw-manifests today would fail its publish with an unknown-subcommand error instead of getting the validation the step claims to perform.
